eval_dimensions.name: Attended Mode Accept/Edit/Reject Gate
eval_dimensions.description: In attended mode, Step 4 fires AskUserQuestion with Accept/Edit/Reject options before returning a story. The draft is never silently accepted or applied without the gate.

eval_dimensions.name: Unattended Mode Skips the Gate
eval_dimensions.description: In unattended mode (release-notes batch generation, commit-title derivation), the skill returns the draft directly without firing AskUserQuestion — the caller owns the batch approval.

eval_dimensions.name: Trace-Upward Actor Selection for Plumbing PRs
eval_dimensions.description: For refactor/infra/dependency-bump PRs, the drafted actor is the user-facing feature's actor traced upward through the dependency chain — never "the developer" as actor.

eval_dimensions.name: Evidence Ranking Over Agent-Written Tickets
eval_dimensions.description: Value claims rest on the diff, PR body, QA comments, and human-sourced quotes before ticket prose; ticket-only claims are tagged [Verify: ticket-only]; comments are read, not just descriptions; one ROI bucket is named with its rejected runner-up (GH-1225).

evals.name: Attended mode fires AskUserQuestion before returning a story
evals.description: Given mode=attended, the skill drafts a story then fires AskUserQuestion (Accept/Edit/Reject) before the story is applied to any target.

assertions.signal: AskUserQuestion fires with Accept / Edit / Reject options showing the drafted story
No inline 'does this story look right?' text substitutes for the widget

evals.name: Reject returns an empty string, not the discarded draft
evals.description: When the user selects Reject at the attended-mode gate, the skill returns an empty string rather than applying the rejected draft anywhere.
evals.input: Dev10x:jtbd invoked with mode=attended; user selects Reject

assertions.signal: Reject selection returns an empty string; the rejected draft is not written to a PR body or ticket

evals.name: Unattended mode returns the draft with no AskUserQuestion
evals.description: When invoked in unattended mode (e.g. by release-notes for a batch of missing JTBDs, or by git-commit for a title derivation), the skill returns the draft directly.

assertions.signal: AskUserQuestion is NOT called; the drafted story string is returned directly to the caller for batching

evals.name: An empty ticket description sends the skill to the comments and the diff
evals.description: GH-1225: the ticket description is empty and the only measured evidence (a declined line lowering the parts subtotal) is in a QA walkthrough comment. The story must cite that, tag anything ticket-only, and name one bucket plus its runner-up.
evals.input: Dev10x:jtbd invoked with mode=unattended, ticket_id=PROJ-706, pr_number=1977

assertions.signal: Comments on the ticket are read, not only the description
The drafted story's outcome is grounded in the QA comment or the diff, and any number carries its source
Exactly one ROI bucket is named, and a one-line rejected runner-up is recorded

evals.name: A system is never the actor or beneficiary
evals.description: GH-1225: the ticket says 'the CRM cannot tell a shop what their staff login is'. The story must name the support rep and the shop owner, not the CRM; for a generated-types-only diff it must story the contract held, not a borrowed outcome.
evals.input: Dev10x:jtbd invoked with mode=unattended, ticket_id=PROJ-724, pr_number=1993

assertions.signal: Story does not contain 'the CRM wants', 'the client wants', or 'so the CRM can'
Because the diff is generated types only, the story names Platform integrity with a counterparty (the backend schema) and records the ticket-level Cost outcome as belonging to the wiring PR

evals.name: A dependency-bump/refactor PR traces upward instead of naming the developer
evals.description: Given a PR that is a pure dependency bump or refactor, the drafted actor is the user-facing feature's actor/beneficiary the plumbing unblocks, never 'the developer'.
evals.input: Dev10x:jtbd invoked with pr_number for a dependency-bump-only PR

assertions.signal: Drafted story does NOT name 'the developer' or 'I' as actor; it traces to a concrete downstream role (e.g., end customer, ops team) per the trace-upward worked example

trigger_evals.description: Queries that should/should-not trigger the jtbd skill (not user-invocable — only via composing skills)

should_trigger.query: Skill(Dev10x:jtbd) invoked by Dev10x:gh-pr-create to source a missing Job Story
should_trigger.rationale: Composed invocation from the PR creation skill — the core use case

should_trigger.query: Skill(Dev10x:jtbd) invoked by Dev10x:release-notes in unattended mode for a batch of PRs
should_trigger.rationale: Composed invocation from release-notes — unattended batch mode

should_not_trigger.query: write a commit message for this change
should_not_trigger.rationale: Commit message formatting — use Dev10x:git-commit (which internally may invoke jtbd for the title, but the user-facing entry point differs)

should_not_trigger.query: the PR already has a Job Story in its description
should_not_trigger.rationale: Story already exists — no drafting needed
